## What does this PR do?

Extend `VarlenDataset` to load the current public `nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-*` text datasets, and stop the packed-sequence data path from stalling the GPU at the start of every training step.

**Datasets**
- Preserve message metadata, tools, and dataset-provided chat-template kwargs. Only the fields a message actually sets reach the chat template; Arrow's `None` placeholders are dropped.
- Map legacy roles to template roles: `developer` -> `system`; legacy `function` replies and Llama `ipython` turns -> `tool`.
- Accept raw pretraining text from `text`, RP2 `raw_content`, and CodeForge `content` fields.
- Normalize OpenAI, legacy function-call, OpenCode tool, structured tool-result, and JSON-encoded Parquet fields.
- Load Hugging Face repos by config and split: the repo's declared default config if there is one, otherwise all configs; per config, `train`, otherwise every split except evaluation splits (`test`, `validation`, `dev`, ...). Several configs/splits are interleaved with a permutation seeded by the dataset `random_seed`, so `--split` ranges and sequential samplers mix them.
- Fall back to a cached map-style JSON payload dataset by reading raw JSONL/Parquet files when Hugging Face Arrow schema casting fails.

**Data loading speed**
- Build varlen samples with numpy/torch instead of Python lists; outputs are byte-identical.
- For training loaders behind a sequence-packing scheduler, set the DataLoader `prefetch_factor` so one global batch stays in flight: the next step's batch is built and pinned while the current step trains. No new argument; other loaders keep the PyTorch default.

## Why?

The existing loader assumed one `train` split and string-only message content. That changed tool-aware tokenization and could not load repositories with thematic splits, OpenCode tool-result blocks, JSON-encoded tool calls, or heterogeneous schemas such as Math-v4.

Packing schedulers pull the whole global batch at the start of every step, while the DataLoader prefetched only 2 items per worker and built each sample as Python lists (~4.6 ms per 50K tokens). On a Qwen3.5 dynamic-CP run (GBS 512, DP 1) the GPU sat idle for ~2.8 s per step waiting for data.

## Scope

This covers the public `nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-*` text repositories (17 repositories and 68 configs/splits as of 2026-10-15), plus RP2 and CodeForge raw-text schemas. Multimodal/VLM datasets remain out of scope for this text-only loader.

## Validation

- Streamed one real Hub sample from all 67 configs/splits across the 16 repositories.
- Normalized and tokenized all 67 samples with the Qwen3-30B-A3B chat template (239 to 104,948 tokens).
- Exercised the raw JSONL/Parquet fallback with real Agentic-v2, Math-v4, and SWE-v3 data.
- Audited all 32,768 rows in the Math-v3 benchmark snapshot and completed the existing fixed-CP4 and dynamic-CP 100-iteration runs without NaNs or skipped iterations.
- Added unit coverage for RP2/CodeForge field detection, alias priority, validation, and local JSONL loading.
- Local CPU-compatible dataset tests: 83 passed, 10 skipped because `datasets` is unavailable, and 6 GPU-dependent tests deselected.
- Tokenizer chat-template metadata forwarding tests: 2 passed.
- Black (26.x), isort (5.13.2), Python 3.11 compile checks, `git diff --check`, and signature verification pass.
- The [previous main CI run](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/33050788126) passed on 2026-08-27, including the data unit-test bucket and linting.
- Review fixes (`61d048d77`..`2c8a442fb`, one commit per finding of the strict review) have unit tests for each finding. Config/split selection is unchanged for all 17 current `nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-*` repositories (68 configs/splits), checked against their Hub metadata; `HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu` now reads only `default`, and `HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k` no longer reads `test_sft`/`test_gen`.
- Real data across the review fixes: the first row of each of the 68 configs/splits (61 streamed, 7 through the raw-file fallback) was normalized before and after the fixes and tokenized with the Qwen3-30B-A3B chat template; token ids are identical for all 68 (239 to 104,948 tokens), including the 8 rows whose messages carried Arrow `None` placeholders.
- Varlen sample construction (`a2bb6861c`): outputs are byte-identical to the previous implementation on 17,472 `VarlenDataset` cases (text, chat and `ChatTemplateSample`; truncation, EOD and `IGNORE_INDEX` at the cut, pad fallback, SBHD and THD) and 384 `MockVarlenDataset` cases; 4.64 ms -> 0.47 ms per 50K-token sample.
- Qwen3.5 proxy (4 layers + MTP, lognormal mean 48K, GBS 512, dynamic CP) on 32 GB200 with the same data-path change, mean of steps 6-20: step start to first forward 2.94 s -> 0.26 s; eager 36.26 s -> 33.65 s per step (-7.2%), chunk-wise CUDA graph 34.96 s -> 32.21 s (-7.9%). Loss and grad norm match the unmodified eager run bit for bit on all 32 ranks over 20 steps.
- Data unit tests before the rebase onto `c3010d6d5` (which leaves the PR's files unchanged) in the MCore CI dev container on 8 x H100 (`test_varlen_dataset.py`, `test_get_batch.py`, `test_sequence_packing.py`, `test_train_step_schedule_plumbing.py`): 413 passed, 113 skipped on every rank (386 passed before these commits). The 2 failures (`test_config_container_forwards_layer_wise_optimizer_to_model_builder`, `args is not initialized`) fail the same way without these commits.
- Black, isort, ruff, pylint (no new messages), `git diff --check`, and signature verification pass for the new commits.

Rebased onto `dev` (`c3010d6d5`) on 2026-10-16; CI requested for `2c8a442fb`.

## Strict review: Nemotron-SFT / RP2 / CodeForge support in the varlen loader

**Findings:** CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 5, SUGGESTION: 0. All five are posted as inline comments, and each one includes a reproducible trigger, a fix, what the fix must not break, and checks to confirm it.

### Most impactful
1. **The Hub loader now changes what you train on, with no error or warning.** Before this PR, [`load_dataset(path, split="train")`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/c75a269efd3fdf6d82ba5a07fff00ed40f350cba/megatron/training/datasets/varlen_dataset.py#L264) loaded only the repo's default config. Now every config is concatenated (`varlen_dataset.py` L519).
   - **Overlapping configs are duplicated.** In `HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu`, `default` already holds every row, and the `sample-*` and per-`CC-MAIN-*` configs repeat subsets of it, so documents get trained on several times.
   - **Test splits are trained on.** When a config has no `train` split, all its splits are used (L521). For `HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k` that means training on `test_sft` and `test_gen`. Before, this case raised an error.
2. **Templates that check whether a key exists now crash.** `dict(m)` (L323) passes through the `None` values Arrow fills in for message fields a row doesn't have. Llama-3.x templates check `'tool_calls' in message`, then call `message.tool_calls|length`, which raises `TypeError` on every user turn. The base code built only `{role, content}`.
3. **Old-style function-calling data now fails.** The assistant's `function_call` is converted to `tool_calls`, but the matching `role: "function"` reply now raises `ValueError` (L309). The same happens to `ipython` turns, which the base code passed through.
4. **Joined configs/splits aren't mixed.** They are concatenated end to end (L590). `--split` takes contiguous index ranges and the `single` sampler reads them in order. So the validation set comes only from the last config/split, and training goes through one topic at a time.

### Overall risk: medium
The tokenizer changes ([`sft_tokenizer.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6c595853b9fb0d2edf257530951c52f0179d477a/megatron/core/tokenizers/text/libraries/sft_tokenizer.py#L130-L167) and [`text_tokenizer.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6c595853b9fb0d2edf257530951c52f0179d477a/megatron/core/tokenizers/text/text_tokenizer.py#L123-L154)) are backward compatible: the new `chat_template_kwargs` argument is optional, keyword-only, and actually used. The masking prompt formats tokenize each turn without the extra kwargs. That is consistent, because their custom templates don't use those kwargs. The RP2/CodeForge text-field aliases and the logic that maps an index to a config/split (including empty ones and negative indices) look correct. I found no unused new arguments, attributes or locals.

The problems are in data selection and normalization. They change what the model trains on without any error, which is the failure this review checks for most. Two of them also break datasets and tokenizers that worked before this PR.

### Scope and limitations
- I reviewed all 5 changed files and traced the affected code paths. For the dataset path, that was `BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder` splitting, `MegatronDataset` indices and `build_pretraining_data_loader` samplers. For the tokenizer path, it was the `MegatronTokenizerText` → `SFTTokenizer` chain.
- I couldn't run anything. The proposed tests and patches are based on reading the source; please verify them before adopting.
- What I say about Hub repo layouts (fineweb-edu, ultrachat_200k) and the Llama-3.x template comes from their public structure; I didn't fetch them.
- I couldn't check the 16 Nemotron-SFT repos. Please compare the selection fixes against the 67 configs/splits you validated.
- The skill points to `style-guide.md`, but it isn't in the base tree, so I skipped the style audit beyond what the linters enforce.

Example: `HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu` (pretrain-text, `text` column) has:
- `default` = `data/*/*`
- `sample-10BT`, `sample-100BT`, `sample-350BT`
- one config per `CC-MAIN-*` dump

Before, each document appeared once. Now each appears at least twice (once in `default`, once in its dump), and documents in the sample configs appear up to 5 times. The corpus is also downloaded several times. There is no error or warning, and a user can't pick a single config.

**Expected.** An `owner/repo` path that worked in the base code still loads the same rows. All configs are combined only when the repo has no default config, which is exactly the case where the base code raised "Config name is missing".

```python
for selected_config in selected_configs:
    ...  # existing split selection
```
`get_dataset_default_config_name` returns:
- the only config, for a single-config repo;
- the config named `default` or marked `default: true`;
- otherwise `None`.

- Single-config repos (e.g. `Yukang/LongAlpaca-12k`) behave the same.
- Multi-config repos without a default still combine all configs.
- How splits are chosen within a config, and the JSON-payload fallback, are unchanged.

- New test: configs `["default", "sample-10BT", "CC-MAIN-2024-10"]`, default `"default"`, each with a `train` split. Expect `calls == [(repo, "default", "train")]`.

**[IMPORTANT Correctness]** When a config has no `train` split, every split is trained on, including test and validation splits

**Failure.** `selected_splits = available_splits` doesn't tell topic splits (like `python`, `cpp`) apart from evaluation splits. Example: `--data-path HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k` has splits `train_sft`, `test_sft`, `train_gen`, `test_gen`. The base code raised `Unknown split "train"`. Now it trains on `test_sft` and `test_gen` without any warning, which contaminates any later evaluation on those sets. The same happens for any repo that has `validation` or `test` but no `train`.

**Expected.** Evaluation splits are never picked up unless explicitly requested.

**Correction** (module helper, plus `import re`):
```python
_EVAL_SPLIT_TOKENS = frozenset({"test", "validation", "valid", "val", "dev", "eval", "evaluation"})


def _is_eval_split(split_name: str) -> bool:
    return any(t in _EVAL_SPLIT_TOKENS for t in re.split(r"[^0-9a-z]+", split_name.lower()))
```
Then replace this line:
```python
if "train" in available_splits:
    selected_splits = ["train"]
else:
    selected_splits = [s for s in available_splits if not _is_eval_split(s)]
    skipped = [s for s in available_splits if _is_eval_split(s)]
    if skipped:
        logger.warning(

            skipped, dataset_path, selected_config,

```
The existing `if not selected_sources: raise ValueError(...)` still catches a repo that has only evaluation splits.

One limitation remains: ultrachat would still load both `train_sft` and `train_gen`, which share prompts. Logging the selected sources helps users notice. The complete fix is a way to select splits explicitly.

**Preservation.**
- A config that has `train` still uses only `train` (e.g. `cfg-a` in the existing test drops `validation`).
- Topic splits like `python` and `cpp` are all still selected.
- Check the 67 Nemotron splits for names that contain these words.

- A single config with only `["validation", "test"]`: raises `ValueError("...no config/split was found...")`.

**[IMPORTANT Compatibility]** `dict(m)` passes Arrow's `None` placeholders through as real message keys, which crashes templates that check whether a key exists

**Failure.** Every loader path here goes through Arrow (`Dataset.from_pandas` and `load_dataset`). Arrow gives all messages the same set of fields: if any message in the data has `tool_calls`, `reasoning_content` or `name`, every message comes back with that key, set to `None` where it was missing. The base code kept only `role` and `content` ([L178-L181](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/c75a269efd3fdf6d82ba5a07fff00ed40f350cba/megatron/training/datasets/varlen_dataset.py#L178-L181)). Now the template receives messages like `{"role": "user", "content": "q", "tool_calls": None}`.

Llama-3.1/3.2/3.3 templates check `'tool_calls' in message` and then evaluate `message.tool_calls|length`. On the first user turn that raises `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()`, so every sample in such a dataset fails in the dataloader.

Minimal trigger: a local JSONL row
```json
{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "q"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "f", "arguments": "{}"}}]}]}
```
with the SFT tokenizer library, the `default` prompt format, and a Llama-3.1 tokenizer.

Same cause, second symptom: the OpenCode `normalized.setdefault("tool_call_id"/"name", ...)` at L326-327 does nothing when Arrow has already put `None` under those keys.

**Expected.** A key in a normalized message means the source row actually set it.

**Correction:**
```suggestion
        normalized = {key: value for key, value in m.items() if value is not None}
```
The same `None` padding happens in `chat_template_kwargs` when it is stored as a struct column. For consistency, replace L369 with `chat_template_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in chat_template_kwargs.items() if v is not None}`.

**Preservation.**
- `content` is set again after the filter, so the Math-v3 assistant `content: None` still becomes `""`.
- Real `tool_calls` lists, `reasoning_content`, `name` and `tool_call_id` are kept.
- The `function_call` → `tool_calls` conversion is unchanged.
- Qwen3 output is unchanged, since that template already treats `None` as missing.

**Acceptance** (proposed test, with `importorskip` for datasets and pandas):
- Run `VarlenLowLevelDataset(_write_jsonl(tmp_path, [row above]))`.
- Expect `set(ll[0].messages[1]) == {"role", "content"}` and `ll[0].messages[2]["tool_calls"][0]["function"]["name"] == "f"`.
- All existing `test_messages_passthrough_*` assertions still hold; for example, the equality in `test_messages_passthrough_decodes_json_encoded_parquet_columns`.

**[IMPORTANT Correctness]** Old-style function-calling conversations are only half converted: the `function` reply turn now raises

**Failure.** L335-348 converts the old-style assistant `function_call` into `tool_calls`. In that format, the reply is `{"role": "function", "name": "python", "content": "2"}`. `"function"` is not in `role_map` or `supported_roles`, so it raises `ValueError: unsupported messages[2] role 'function'` in `__getitem__` and stops the dataloader.

The base code passed this role through. It did the same for Llama-3.1 `ipython` tool-result turns, which now raise too. `_SHAREGPT_ROLE_MAP` in this file already maps `function` and `observation` to `tool`.

**Expected.** Old-style reply turns become `tool` turns.

**Correction:**
```suggestion
    role_map = {"developer": "system", "function": "tool", "ipython": "tool"}
```

**[IMPORTANT Correctness]** Configs and splits are concatenated end to end, so `--split` ranges and the sequential sampler see one component at a time

**Failure.** The global index runs through one component after another: all of the first config/split, then all of the next. Nothing later in the pipeline reorders it:
- `_build_megatron_dataset_splits` gives each train/valid/test split a contiguous `numpy.arange(beg, end)` range ([L475-L477](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6c595853b9fb0d2edf257530951c52f0179d477a/megatron/core/datasets/blended_megatron_dataset_builder.py#L475-L477)).
- `MegatronDataset` keeps the indices as given.
- `--dataloader-type single` (`MegatronPretrainingSampler`) reads them in order.

Example: a repo with topic splits `[python, cpp]` and `--split 99,1,0`. The validation set is the last 1% of rows, so it is all cpp. Training reads every python sample, then every cpp sample. That is a topic-by-topic curriculum nobody asked for, and nothing reports it. The base code loaded a single component, so this didn't happen.

**Expected.** Any contiguous range of indices is an even mix of components, and the order is identical on every rank.

**Correction** (a sketch; how the seed gets passed in is up to you):

- Single-component loads (local JSONL/parquet, Hub repos with a single split) keep the base row order.
- Building without a seed (as the existing Hub test does) keeps the concatenated order, so its `low_level[0]`, `[1]` and `[-1]` assertions still hold.

**Acceptance** (proposed test): two fake components of 50 rows each, `shuffle_seed=1234`. Expect:
- the contents of `ll[i]` for `i in range(100)` are exactly the 100 rows, each once;
- `ll[90]` to `ll[99]` include rows from both components;
- two instances built with the same seed return the same order.

detail.body:
## What does this PR do?

Extend `VarlenDataset` to load the current public `nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-*` text datasets, and stop the packed-sequence data path from stalling the GPU at the start of every training step.

**Datasets**
- Preserve message metadata, tools, and dataset-provided chat-template kwargs. Only the fields a message actually sets reach the chat template; Arrow's `None` placeholders are dropped.
- Map legacy roles to template roles: `developer` -> `system`; legacy `function` replies and Llama `ipython` turns -> `tool`.
- Accept raw pretraining text from `text`, RP2 `raw_content`, and CodeForge `content` fields.
- Normalize OpenAI, legacy function-call, OpenCode tool, structured tool-result, and JSON-encoded Parquet fields.
- Load Hugging Face repos by config and split: the repo's declared default config if there is one, otherwise all configs; per config, `train`, otherwise every split except evaluation splits (`test`, `validation`, `dev`, ...). Several configs/splits are interleaved with a permutation seeded by the dataset `random_seed`, so `--split` ranges and sequential samplers mix them.
- Fall back to a cached map-style JSON payload dataset by reading raw JSONL/Parquet files when Hugging Face Arrow schema casting fails.

**Data loading speed**
- Build varlen samples with numpy/torch instead of Python lists; outputs are byte-identical.
- For training loaders behind a sequence-packing scheduler, set the DataLoader `prefetch_factor` so one global batch stays in flight: the next step's batch is built and pinned while the current step trains. No new argument; other loaders keep the PyTorch default.

## Why?

The existing loader assumed one `train` split and string-only message content. That changed tool-aware tokenization and could not load repositories with thematic splits, OpenCode tool-result blocks, JSON-encoded tool calls, or heterogeneous schemas such as Math-v4.

Packing schedulers pull the whole global batch at the start of every step, while the DataLoader prefetched only 2 items per worker and built each sample as Python lists (~4.6 ms per 50K tokens). On a Qwen3.5 dynamic-CP run (GBS 512, DP 1) the GPU sat idle for ~2.8 s per step waiting for data.

## Scope

This covers the public `nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-*` text repositories (17 repositories and 68 configs/splits as of 2026-10-15), plus RP2 and CodeForge raw-text schemas. Multimodal/VLM datasets remain out of scope for this text-only loader.

## Validation

- Streamed one real Hub sample from all 67 configs/splits across the 16 repositories.
- Normalized and tokenized all 67 samples with the Qwen3-30B-A3B chat template (239 to 104,948 tokens).
- Exercised the raw JSONL/Parquet fallback with real Agentic-v2, Math-v4, and SWE-v3 data.
- Audited all 32,768 rows in the Math-v3 benchmark snapshot and completed the existing fixed-CP4 and dynamic-CP 100-iteration runs without NaNs or skipped iterations.
- Added unit coverage for RP2/CodeForge field detection, alias priority, validation, and local JSONL loading.
- Local CPU-compatible dataset tests: 83 passed, 10 skipped because `datasets` is unavailable, and 6 GPU-dependent tests deselected.
- Tokenizer chat-template metadata forwarding tests: 2 passed.
- Black (26.x), isort (5.13.2), Python 3.11 compile checks, `git diff --check`, and signature verification pass.
- The [previous main CI run](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/33050788126) passed on 2026-08-27, including the data unit-test bucket and linting.
- Review fixes (`61d048d77`..`2c8a442fb`, one commit per finding of the strict review) have unit tests for each finding. Config/split selection is unchanged for all 17 current `nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-*` repositories (68 configs/splits), checked against their Hub metadata; `HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu` now reads only `default`, and `HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k` no longer reads `test_sft`/`test_gen`.
- Real data across the review fixes: the first row of each of the 68 configs/splits (61 streamed, 7 through the raw-file fallback) was normalized before and after the fixes and tokenized with the Qwen3-30B-A3B chat template; token ids are identical for all 68 (239 to 104,948 tokens), including the 8 rows whose messages carried Arrow `None` placeholders.
- Varlen sample construction (`a2bb6861c`): outputs are byte-identical to the previous implementation on 17,472 `VarlenDataset` cases (text, chat and `ChatTemplateSample`; truncation, EOD and `IGNORE_INDEX` at the cut, pad fallback, SBHD and THD) and 384 `MockVarlenDataset` cases; 4.64 ms -> 0.47 ms per 50K-token sample.
- Qwen3.5 proxy (4 layers + MTP, lognormal mean 48K, GBS 512, dynamic CP) on 32 GB200 with the same data-path change, mean of steps 6-20: step start to first forward 2.94 s -> 0.26 s; eager 36.26 s -> 33.65 s per step (-7.2%), chunk-wise CUDA graph 34.96 s -> 32.21 s (-7.9%). Loss and grad norm match the unmodified eager run bit for bit on all 32 ranks over 20 steps.
- Data unit tests before the rebase onto `c3010d6d5` (which leaves the PR's files unchanged) in the MCore CI dev container on 8 x H100 (`test_varlen_dataset.py`, `test_get_batch.py`, `test_sequence_packing.py`, `test_train_step_schedule_plumbing.py`): 413 passed, 113 skipped on every rank (386 passed before these commits). The 2 failures (`test_config_container_forwards_layer_wise_optimizer_to_model_builder`, `args is not initialized`) fail the same way without these commits.
- Black, isort, ruff, pylint (no new messages), `git diff --check`, and signature verification pass for the new commits.

Rebased onto `dev` (`c3010d6d5`) on 2026-10-16; CI requested for `2c8a442fb`.

**Failure.** Every loader path here goes through Arrow (`Dataset.from_pandas` and `load_dataset`). Arrow gives all messages the same set of fields: if any message in the data has `tool_calls`, `reasoning_content` or `name`, every message comes back with that key, set to `None` where it was missing. The base code kept only `role` and `content` ([L178-L181](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/c75a269efd3fdf6d82ba5a07fff00ed40f350cba/megatron/training/datasets/varlen_dataset.py#L178-L181)). Now the template receives messages like `{"role": "user", "content": "q", "tool_calls": None}`.

Llama-3.1/3.2/3.3 templates check `'tool_calls' in message` and then evaluate `message.tool_calls|length`. On the first user turn that raises `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()`, so every sample in such a dataset fails in the dataloader.


<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=moderate -->

## Strict review: Nemotron-SFT / RP2 / CodeForge support in the varlen loader

**Findings:** CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 5, SUGGESTION: 0. All five are posted as inline comments, and each one includes a reproducible trigger, a fix, what the fix must not break, and checks to confirm it.

### Most impactful
1. **The Hub loader now changes what you train on, with no error or warning.** Before this PR, [`load_dataset(path, split="train")`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/c75a269efd3fdf6d82ba5a07fff00ed40f350cba/megatron/training/datasets/varlen_dataset.py#L264) loaded only the repo's default config. Now every config is concatenated (`varlen_dataset.py` L519).
   - **Overlapping configs are duplicated.** In `HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu`, `default` already holds every row, and the `sample-*` and per-`CC-MAIN-*` configs repeat subsets of it, so documents get trained on several times.
   - **Test splits are trained on.** When a config has no `train` split, all its splits are used (L521). For `HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k` that means training on `test_sft` and `test_gen`. Before, this case raised an error.
2. **Templates that check whether a key exists now crash.** `dict(m)` (L323) passes through the `None` values Arrow fills in for message fields a row doesn't have. Llama-3.x templates check `'tool_calls' in message`, then call `message.tool_calls|length`, which raises `TypeError` on every user turn. The base code built only `{role, content}`.
3. **Old-style function-calling data now fails.** The assistant's `function_call` is converted to `tool_calls`, but the matching `role: "function"` reply now raises `ValueError` (L309). The same happens to `ipython` turns, which the base code passed through.
4. **Joined configs/splits aren't mixed.** They are concatenated end to end (L590). `--split` takes contiguous index ranges and the `single` sampler reads them in order. So the validation set comes only from the last config/split, and training goes through one topic at a time.

### Overall risk: medium
The tokenizer changes ([`sft_tokenizer.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6c595853b9fb0d2edf257530951c52f0179d477a/megatron/core/tokenizers/text/libraries/sft_tokenizer.py#L130-L167) and [`text_tokenizer.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6c595853b9fb0d2edf257530951c52f0179d477a/megatron/core/tokenizers/text/text_tokenizer.py#L123-L154)) are backward compatible: the new `chat_template_kwargs` argument is optional, keyword-only, and actually used. The masking prompt formats tokenize each turn without the extra kwargs. That is consistent, because their custom templates don't use those kwargs. The RP2/CodeForge text-field aliases and the logic that maps an index to a config/split (including empty ones and negative indices) look correct. I found no unused new arguments, attributes or locals.

The problems are in data selection and normalization. They change what the model trains on without any error, which is the failure this review checks for most. Two of them also break datasets and tokenizers that worked before this PR.

### Scope and limitations
- I reviewed all 5 changed files and traced the affected code paths. For the dataset path, that was `BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder` splitting, `MegatronDataset` indices and `build_pretraining_data_loader` samplers. For the tokenizer path, it was the `MegatronTokenizerText` → `SFTTokenizer` chain.
- I couldn't run anything. The proposed tests and patches are based on reading the source; please verify them before adopting.
- What I say about Hub repo layouts (fineweb-edu, ultrachat_200k) and the Llama-3.x template comes from their public structure; I didn't fetch them.
- I couldn't check the 16 Nemotron-SFT repos. Please compare the selection fixes against the 67 configs/splits you validated.
- The skill points to `style-guide.md`, but it isn't in the base tree, so I skipped the style audit beyond what the linters enforce.
